abortedRuns.observed: Aborting batchmode due to failure: Scripts have compiler errors.
abortedRuns.cause: The LiveKit SDK package cache held 130-133 byte Git-LFS pointer stubs for its desktop binaries (Google.Protobuf.dll declared size 472864), so the package did not compile: 3645x CS0538, 117x CS0400, 24x CS0246. No test discovery happened; no XML was produced.
abortedRuns.resolution: Resolved locally without any network transfer: the seven desktop binaries pinned by foundation/network/dependency-contract.json were copied from a sibling local checkout of the same repository and verified against the contract sha256/size, then the repository script scripts/dev/prepare_multiplayer_dependencies.py --apply reported nothing missing and applied its reviewed Pipeline asmdef patch. Its verify mode then returned dependency_files_verified for all seven binaries.
abortedRuns.note: This run is a refused/aborted run, not a skip observation, and is kept unmodified.

discoveryBoundary.finding: Repeating -testFilter does not union: the last filter wins. run-20260914T1745-pair-pre was launched with FoundationSimulationTests and WorldMotionAdapterTests as two -testFilter arguments and discovered only the 70 WorldMotionAdapterTests cases.
discoveryBoundary.consequence: the pairing design was inconclusive and was not used as pairing evidence; a single regex alternation filter was used instead.

discoveryBoundary.finding: -testFilter accepts a regular-expression alternation and then unions the matching classes.

cause.summary: A cross-fixture scene-dirt leak, not a discovery failure and not a broken test. MultiplayerSceneTests leaves the generated scene it built open and dirty, so the next dirty-scene guard in the assembly - WorldMotionAdapterTests.[OneTimeSetUp] - refuses to run and NUnit reports its 70 cases as Skipped with the guard message.
cause.observedBy: run-20260914T1745-probe-scene, a temporary probe fixture run between MultiplayerSceneTests and WorldMotionAdapterTests; the probe file itself was deleted before the commit and only its receipt is kept.
chain: MultiplayerSceneTests calls MultiplayerSceneBuilder.Build(path), which calls FoundationDemoSceneBuilder.Build.

FoundationDemoSceneBuilder computes replaceUntitled = sceneCount == 1 && the single scene has an empty path, which is exactly the batchmode startup scene, and therefore calls NewScene(EmptyScene, NewSceneMode.Single): the startup scene is destroyed and the generated scene becomes the only loaded scene.

The test finally block closes only scenes whose path starts with the build path. That scene is now the last loaded scene, so EditorSceneManager.CloseScene cannot remove it and the close silently leaves it open (its return value is not checked).
AssetDatabase.DeleteAsset(path) then deletes the asset that backs the still-open scene, which leaves the scene marked dirty.
SceneManager.SetActiveScene(previous) is skipped because the startup scene captured at the top was already destroyed, so nothing restores the editor.
The editor is left holding one loaded dirty scene; every later fixture that guards on Scene.isDirty in [OneTimeSetUp] or [SetUp] then calls Assert.Ignore and reports entirely as Skipped.
cause.whyItIsAnEnvironmentCause: The guard is correct and intentional: it protects unsaved user work. The defect is that a fixture leaked its build scene into the shared editor state, so the guard fired for a reason that has nothing to do with the 70 cases.
excludedCandidates: VoiceEpochCoordinatorTests creates ~40 GameObjects in the active scene but destroys them all and does not pollute: Voice + WorldMotion pass together (run-20260914T1745-pair-voice-pre).
FoundationSimulationTests and GroundedActorGeometryTests are not necessary: bisectA reproduces the 70 skips without them.
The journal and snapshot fixtures (ShiftJournalTests, SimulationJournalTests, SnapshotFreshnessTests) do not touch scenes at all: bisectD passes 169/169.
NativeSdkImportTests only reads an AssetImporter and cannot dirty a scene; it is present in bisectC only because it shares the same neighbourhood, and its failure is a separate required regression.

fix.kind: test hygiene fix on the polluter fixture only; no guard, no test and no Ignore was removed or weakened
fix.change: In the test finally block, after the existing close/delete/SetActiveScene cleanup, if any loaded scene is still dirty, replace it with a clean untitled scene via EditorSceneManager.NewScene(NewSceneSetup.EmptyScene, NewSceneMode.Single). The test body, its assertions and its dirty-scene refusal guard are untouched.

controlledReproductionAfter.note: WorldMotionAdapterTests runs all 70 and passes; the 1 remaining failure is the NativeSdkImportTests required regression, not a skip.

fullSuiteAfter.note: the 70 skips are gone because the 70 cases executed; the 5 remaining skips are exactly the intentional preservation guards, and the 2 failures are unchanged required regressions. total is unchanged at 500, so nothing was dropped or hidden.

fix.followsExistingRepoRemedy: The repository already uses exactly this remedy where the captured previous scene may be gone: Packages/com.xrlab.chooguard.foundation/Demo/Tests/Editor/StationWorldSceneTests.cs [TearDown] and ReconstructionReviewTests.cs both fall back to EditorSceneManager.NewScene(NewSceneSetup.EmptyScene, NewSceneMode.Single) when previous.IsValid() is false. MultiplayerSceneTests had that fallback only for SetActiveScene and never restored a clean scene.
fix.notChangedOnPurpose: the seven Editor dirty-scene guards, the SceneBuilderTests Directory.Exists guards, the ReconstructionReviewTests File.Exists guard and the four [Test, Explicit] attributes are all intentional and were left exactly as they were.
